analyst_view.overall: Early view: Inter visit Frosinone four days before a Champions League trip to Borussia Dortmund. Lautaro has been out with a muscle injury since 15 October and Bonny was hurt against Como, so Inter's striker options may still be thin. Frosinone are sixth with an attacking, high-pressing style; Bracaglia, listed as suspended, will have served his one-match ban at Milan, and top scorer Raimondo's fitness after going off at Cagliari is the main question.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.8 goals, the highest in this group. I lean slightly lower: Inter's away games have averaged three goals, and Inter concede little, about 1.2 a game. Frosinone's home games do average 3.7, so I would not go far below the number.

corners.text: The site expects 10.3 corners. I lean slightly higher: Frosinone's home games have averaged about 12 corners, and Inter's away games about ten. Frosinone attack down the wings, and Inter win six corners a game themselves.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.2 cards. I lean higher, because Inter's away games have averaged over four cards and Frosinone's home games almost four. Frosinone press aggressively, and that leads to fouls against a quick Inter side.

shots.text: The site expects 34.0 shots, which is very high but fits: Frosinone's home games have averaged about 36 shots and Inter's away games about 31. Both sides like to shoot, so I stay with the number.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.9 shots on target. Frosinone's home games have averaged over 12 on target and Inter's away games about nine, which lands on the number. I see nothing that points either way.
